_meta.what_this_is: An SLO and two error scenarios. The SLO (99.9% success over a 30-day window) allows an error budget of 0.1% of requests. Burn rate is how fast a scenario spends that budget: error_rate / error_budget. A raw-threshold alert fires when the instantaneous error rate exceeds a fixed level; it catches a loud FAST burn but misses a quiet SLOW burn that sits just under the threshold yet runs long enough to exhaust the whole budget. Burn-rate alerting fires on both, because it measures budget consumption, not instantaneous rate.
_meta.data_is: A FIXTURE. The SLO, window, alert thresholds, and the two scenarios (a 5% fast burn for 2 hours; a 0.3% slow burn for the whole month) are hand-authored so the slow burn exhausts 300% of the budget while sitting below the 1% raw-alert threshold, and the fast burn eats 14% of the month budget in 2 hours. Every burn rate and budget figure is computed in burn.py.
_meta.format: slo; window_hours; raw_alert_rate: the instantaneous error rate a raw alert fires at; scenarios: {name: {error_rate, hours}}.
